profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. In December 2017, Iron Mountain agreed to acquire IO Data Centers' US division for roughly 1.3 billion dollars, a deal that closed in January 2018 and added four colocation data centers in New Jersey, Ohio, and two in Arizona, per Wikipedia's account of the transaction.

This facility, at 3003 Woodbridge Avenue in Edison, New Jersey, is that acquired New Jersey site. It carries the legacy name "IO Datacenter" in some third-party mapping data, a holdover from before Iron Mountain's rebrand; the operator's own current site no longer uses the IO name, referring to the facility simply as its New Jersey location, internally designated NJE-1. This registry corrects a mapping-data postal code error found on this row: 07054 is Florham Park, New Jersey, not Edison; the operator's own site confirms Edison's correct 08837 zip code for this address, which has been applied here along with a former_operator record for IO Data Centers rather than deleting that history.

Per the operator's own site, NJE-1 spans 830,000 square feet on a 43-acre campus, with 30 MW of IT power capacity under 2N redundancy, TIA-942 certification, more than 22 network carriers on site, and more than 18,000 rooftop solar panels, which Iron Mountain describes as the largest such installation at any North American data center. The site sits roughly 30 miles from Manhattan. This registry has not located a primary source specifying the year this building was originally constructed by IO Data Centers prior to the 2018 acquisition; that detail is left unconfirmed rather than estimated.

Iron Mountain trades on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker IRM and files with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under CIK 0001020569, structured as a real estate investment trust. Records management remains the company's larger, founding business line by facility count; the data center segment is reported separately in Iron Mountain's public filings as a smaller but faster-growing division, of which NJE-1 is the company's sole currently marketed New Jersey site.

reading.body:
The Iron Mountain New Jersey campus in Edison carries 30 MW of IT power capacity on a 43-acre footprint with TIA-942 certification, qualifying it for general enterprise and colocation workloads. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, a common density, 30 MW of IT load translates to roughly 750 racks. The campus connects to more than 22 network carriers and operates the largest rooftop solar installation documented at any North American data center, though solar output capacity is not published.

Among the five New Jersey facilities with published power figures tracked by this site, NJE-1 ranks sixth by capacity, which indicates it is below the state's largest published site. New Jersey's five publicly specified facilities total 111.3 MW of IT power, meaning this campus represents 27 percent of the state's published AI-scale data center capacity that has disclosed specifications to the public.

This site sits 30 miles from Manhattan and was acquired by Iron Mountain from IO Data Centers in January 2018 as part of a larger US portfolio purchase. Iron Mountain has since rebranded the facility as its New Jersey location and markets it as its sole current New Jersey data center offering. The company reports data centers as a separate, faster-growing segment within its business, distinct from its larger records-management division.
